transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’m constantly trying to make up for what I eat with these intense workouts and routines, and it’s really taking over my life. I'm just so exhausted from this constant cycle, and it's starting to get in the way of everything I'm trying to achieve.
Can you describe your eating habits and how you feel about food, and do you ever find yourself restricting food intake or purging after eating?

After late shifts, I completely lose control and plow through huge amounts of leftover concession food, like burgers, fries, and churros, until I'm painfully full. I feel so guilty afterward that I force myself to throw up over the bathroom sink to try and undo the damage. On my days off, I also drag myself through punishing hikes and extra hours at the gym to try to erase what I ate.
Can you estimate how often you engage in these binge-eating episodes followed by purging, and do you also restrict your food intake on days when you don't binge?

This cycle of bingeing and then trying to undo it happens at least once a week, and it's been going on regularly for several months now. I don't really restrict or starve myself on other days; I just rely on throwing up right after I overeat or forcing myself through those brutal workouts to try to erase it.
Have you noticed any significant fluctuations in your weight over the past few months despite your efforts to compensate for binge eating?
I haven't really noticed any major weight fluctuations, so I'm not entirely sure. I mostly just obsess and panic over even a single pound change on the scale, rather than seeing any big ups or downs.
Do you fear gaining weight or becoming fat, even when you're at a healthy weight, and does this fear influence your decision to purge or engage in excessive exercise after binge-eating episodes?

Yes, I have a massive fear of gaining weight. If the scale goes up even a pound or my work polo feels tight, I panic about looking like the out-of-shape old guy at the park that no one takes seriously. That fear is exactly what drives me to throw up after a binge or force myself through those brutal workouts to erase the food.
